ios.desc:
Features:
• Pitch accent information
• Dictionaries that update automatically every week fetching just the updated entries
• Recognition of a wide range of grammatical forms
• Conversion of yen amounts (e.g. 100億円)
• Translation of Japanese-era years into Gregorian years (e.g. 昭和５６年)
• Automatic preview of names
• Support for displaying romaji
• Support for vertical text and text in SVG images
• Support for non-English dictionaries (unfortunately no Japanese-Japanese dictionary is freely available yet)
• Up-to-date kanji data including educational and kanji kentei levels, reworked kanji components etc.
• Many settings to customize to your needs
• Localization into Simplified Chinese and Japanese

How to use:
• After installing the app it will begin downloading the dictionaries in the background. You may have to wait a few minutes before all the data is fully available.
• To look up words on a Web page, enable the extension from the Safari menu then drag the "10." circle to the word you wish to look up.
• Tap the circle once to disable looking up. Tap it again to re-enable.
• Double-tap the circle to switch its direction.
• Tap the tabs to view kanji or name information.

For Japanese, the browser extensions Yomichan[0] (Chrome-clones and Firefox) and 10ten[1] (Safari macOS/iOS, Chrome-clones, Firefox) function similarly. There’s also several community-built tools that are made to work with these extensions like mokuro[2] and subadub[3].

[0]: https://foosoft.net/projects/yomichan/
[1]: https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/10ten-japanese-reader-rik/pnmaklegiibbioifkmfkgpfnmdehdfan, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/10ten-japanese-reader/id1573540634, https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/10ten-ja-reader/
[2]: https://github.com/kha-white/mokuro
[3]: https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/subadub/jamiekdimmhnnemaaimmdahnahfmfdfk, https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/subadub/
quotes.story_title: Show HN: Kimchi Reader – Immersive Korean Learning with a Popup Dictionary
